messages:
Marie: quick heads-up — during the private deploy run I noticed adapters injecting three extra handshake fields (identity_policy, tenant_tags, secret_rebind) upstream. That makes the hosted adapter validation path stricter than necessary. Can we discuss whether the controlplane should handle these as optional or we keep explicit capabilities per mode?
AJ: @Marie thanks for surfacing. My quick take: prefer a minimal stable handshake and add an optional 'capabilities' probe. Avoid embedding mode-specific fields in core contract.
Devon: +1 on minimal contract. Concern: optional capabilities means older adapters may not advertise critical things (e.g., secret_rebind). How do we prevent silent degradation during rollouts?
Samira: we ran into that exact failure in staging — private -> hosted fallback happened because secret_rebind wasn't advertised, and runtime tried to bind a KMS key that wasn't available. It produced a 502 cascade.
AJ: suggestion: two-phase: (1) lightweight probe at attach-time returning capability flags, (2) periodic heartbeat with capability deltas. Probe example in pseudocode: 
```
POST /adapter/probe 200
{
  "capabilities": ["secret_rebind","kv_cache_v2"],
  "max_seq_len": 2048
}
```
If probe fails, treat adapter as "compat_mode=best_effort" and route to a more conservative path.
Devon: routing to conservative path is fine, but we need a clear metric and alert: if probe missing for X% of requests, trigger rollback or canary halt. Otherwise SLAs silently suffer.
Marie: agree. Also thinking about long-term: adapters should expose a capability schema version (cap_schema_v) so we can evolve flags without breaking.
Samira: operational note — private deployments often carry custom sidecars that add capabilities; they don't always update the controlplane. So defaulting to conservative is safe but costly. We should provide a cost-visibility signal in the console when falling back.
AJ: +1 for console signal. Add rollout policy: if canary nodes advertise capability=false, abort rollout. Maybe implement a gate in the Console: "require_probe_success=true" for critical features.
Devon: one more tradeoff — if we push too much probing, we increase attach latency. Can we make probe async and cache results with TTL?
AJ: yes: async probe with cached TTL + immediate best-effort route. On first attach, route to conservative path until probe completes. Cache TTL configurable per tenant.
Samira: here's an ugly edge we hit: secret_rebind requires transient KMS creds for the probe itself. That means probes can fail due to auth races. Need retry/backoff and clear error codes so controlplane knows "probe failed due to auth" vs "capability absent".
Marie: agreed — separate failure codes: 428 (probe-auth-required), 204 (no-capability), 200 (has-capability). Also log detailed probe-reason to console for troubleshooting.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for adapter-v3 scheduled at 2024-11-07T18:12:00Z — note: probes enabled by default in canary.
Devon: Thanks ops-bot — we should pause that canary until we add the TTL-cache + probe failure metrics.
AJ: action items: 1) implement probe endpoint + schema version (owner: AJ), 2) add probe TTL/cache and conservative routing (owner: Devon), 3) console signal + rollout gate (owner: Samira), 4) standardized probe error codes + doc (owner: Marie).
Marie: timeline? can we aim for prototype in 2 weeks so we can unpause canary?
Samira: ok for 2 weeks but need help from infra to add an ephemeral KMS test harness for probes.
Devon: will draft the routing fallback throttles and alerts — will post a follow-up thread with thresholds.
AJ: I'll create the RFC PR today with probe schema and example payloads.
Marie: great. Thanks all. We'll keep this thread as the short-term sync. If anyone hits a regression, ping here and tag @oncall. :thumbsup:
